A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RIFLEx study. Their readable main text, Appendices A–F, equations, three tables, and 13 figures support reliable comparison despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation evaluations and user-study results in Table 1, alongside frequency analyses, ablations, and generated examples.

after.justification: v2 retains original quantitative evaluations, user-study outcomes, frequency ablations, and qualitative generation results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Intrinsic-frequency identification and reduction remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 now explicitly writes the assignment 2π/(Ls), replacing an equation reference; this assignment was already specified in v1 Section 3.3.

E1.justification: Both retain the private video data, VBench and HunyuanVideo prompt evaluations, and temporal, spatial, and joint extrapolation scenarios. Newly discussed autoregressive and efficient-attention models introduce no evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains PE, NTK, PI, TASR, and YaRN in the corresponding training-free comparisons, PE in fine-tuning comparisons, and NTK in the HunyuanVideo 2.3× comparison. Appendix comparator membership is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix D retain the evaluation metrics, 100 HunyuanVideo prompts, 10 user-study participants, ranking and tie rules, and NoRepeat threshold of 100. Table 3 training budgets, batch sizes, resolutions, and frequency settings are identical.

E4.justification: The frequency-isolation analysis, fine-tuning comparison, 4× failure example, and Appendix E robustness and frequency ablations are retained unchanged. Expanded explanatory discussion adds no new analytical evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The user-study and 20-video intrinsic-frequency robustness sample descriptions remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 scores, rankings, and preference percentages are identical, and the figure results are retained. For example, training-free HunyuanVideo 2.3× NoRepeat scores remain 20.0 for NTK and 54.0 for RIFLEx.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(8), including the intrinsic-frequency definition and non-repetition condition, are mathematically unchanged. Explaining index j and restating the update in Algorithm 1 add clarification without new definitions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central intrinsic-frequency contribution and claims of training-free 2× extrapolation and fine-tuned 3× extrapolation without long-video training. Spatial and joint extensions were already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 adds an explanation of quality loss through training–inference positional-embedding mismatch. Section 5 expands the brief training-from-scratch caveat into limitations concerning visual frequency identification and missing theoretical foundations. Section 4.2 and Appendix A add applicability reasoning.

D1.justification: Section 5 explicitly discloses visual inspection as the principal approach to intrinsic-frequency identification, whereas v1 referred to observed repetitions without specifying this. This clarifies the existing procedure; Table 3 implementation settings and Table 2 code/license information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix A substantially broadens positioning with a dedicated discussion of autoregressive video generation, including NUWA, VideoPoet, repetition limitations, and potential relevance of RIFLEx’s periodicity analysis. It also adds SageAttention, SageAttention2, and SpargeAttn, extending the previous RoPE and diffusion-focused coverage.

P1.justification: Localized explanatory additions revise Sections 3.2–3.3, 4.2, and 5, and expand Appendix A. Affiliations and publication text are updated and acknowledgements added. Most prose and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The same figures and tables retain their content and structure, but appendix floats are redistributed. Figures 11 and 12, previously together, are separated; Figure 13 occupies its own page, and Tables 2 and 3 move relative to surrounding text.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency by explicitly acknowledging visual frequency selection and its unresolved theoretical basis, while clarifying extrapolation limits and broadening relevant context in Appendix A. These help readers assess the unchanged method and evidence. The gain is limited: broader applicability suggestions receive no new experimental validation.
